He concurs with our diagnosis. He adds: "The sections of this core biopsy specimen display a background of fibrocystic changes and microcalcifications. I acknowledge that the cells lining the small duct and terminal duct-lobular units in block "1" appear crowded and have columnar shapes, but I would not classify the focus as atypical ductal hyperplasia of columnar cell type. The glands display a branching of serrated configuration, and the myoepithelial cell layer appears especially prominent. Acini altered by genuine atypical columnar hyperplasia usually have round or globular shapes and inconspicuous myoepithelial cells. I suspect that the marked focus in this case at hand represents blunt duct adenosis, the lesion most difficult to distinguish from atypical ductal hyperplasia of columnar cell type. I believe that one of the dotted foci in block "2" also represents blunt duct adenosis." Final Diagnosis by: Nicole A.
